author: The Wall Street Journal
description:
When Evan Gershkovich was arrested by Russia’s security forces in 2023—the first U.S. journalist charged with espionage in the country since the Cold War—he never stopped reporting.

Now, sitting down with Evan ahead of the release of his book, “This Cursed Beautiful Land,” WSJ editor in chief Emma Tucker listened as he recalled the “pure fear” of his arrest—and how he survived over a year in Moscow’s infamous Lefortovo prison.

Chapters:
0:00 Evan’s arrest
0:37 How you got through 16 months in prison
1:24 Keeping copies of your notes in prison
2:20 The day of the arrest and hostage diplomacy
3:53 Reporting from the inside
4:48 Were you able to consume Western media?
6:24 Negotiations for Evan’s release and Navalny
7:10 Evan’s lowest point and the trial
9:00 Evan’s release and arriving back on American soil
10:55 The state of journalism today

title: How Evan Gershkovich Kept Reporting From Inside a Russian Prison | WSJ

author: The Wall Street Journal
description:
At the Mountain School, families pay $40,000 a semester for their teens to do chores on a farm in rural Vermont. Their goal: Students learn to appreciate the people doing these tasks in every community.⁠
⁠
Some students and alums consider the Mountain School a secret path to top colleges. Other families are seeking a wider perspective beyond traditional schooling and a rare reprieve from technology.⁠

title: Inside the School Where Teens Do Farmwork for $40K a Semester
